column1: # Photoshop's DEFAULT keyboard shortcuts (Windows and macOS), as test data for
# Source: Adobe, "Default keyboard shortcuts in Adobe Photoshop",
# shortcuts, Function keys, Keys for selecting tools, Keys for viewing images, Keys for selecting
# and moving objects, Keys for transforming selections, Keys for painting objects, Keys for
# blending modes, Keys for the Layers panel, Keys for using panels), cross-checked against the
# shortcuts Photoshop's own menus print. Used only as a list of facts (which key does what); no
# text, code or assets were copied. (On 2026-10-10 helpx.adobe.com answered 403 to this build
# server and the Wayback copy was rate-limited, so the rows were transcribed from the list as
# published and from Photoshop's menus; re-check them against the page when it is reachable.)
# Columns (tab-separated): area, action, Windows keys, macOS keys, what Capishot must do.
# Keys are written the way Adobe writes them (Ctrl/Alt on Windows, Command/Option on macOS;
# "Delete" on macOS is the Mac's delete key, i.e. Backspace). The last column is checked by
# pressing the key through the real shortcut handler (`shortcuts::handle`):
#   cmd:<id>         the press dispatches this command (dry run; disabled still counts)
#   tool:<Tool>      the press selects a tool of that tool's group
#   cycle:<Tool>     with that tool current, the press switches to another tool of its group
#   hold:<id>        the temporary (held) tool with that binding id is on this key
#   opacity:<n>      with the Brush, the press sets its opacity to n %
#   flow:<n>         with the Brush, the press sets its flow to n %
#   blend:<mode>     with the Move tool, the press sets the active layer's blend mode
#   brushblend:<m>   with the Brush, the press sets the brush's blend mode
#   transform:<what> during Free Transform, the press commits or cancels it
#   nudge:<px>       with the Move tool, the press moves the active layer right by px
